changes.reason: Handbook 9.4: a unit heats to the case supply temperature plus a supply_margin that covers the losses after it. The 5 km supply main is the loss after the unit; with the insulation below the residual drop is about a third of the 2 K margin, so 3 K leaves headroom for the lead's wider pipe (UA grows with the diameter) and for ground-temperature and fouling drift. The heat pump and the boiler carry the same margin so the boiler stays idle off-peak instead of lifting 1 K on every step. The exact consumer temperature is the pipe evaluation below.

Same margin as the heat pump (handbook 9.4): the boiler sits directly upstream of the supply main, so it must deliver the same 103 degC outlet as the heat pump; a smaller margin would make it burn gas to lift the heat pump's outlet by a kelvin on every step, a larger one would raise the peak-day temperature for nothing.

Design value for a pre-insulated district-heating transmission main: steel carrier pipe, thick polyurethane foam, HDPE jacket, laid in dry sand bedding. The stored 1 W/m2/K is a bare or thinly insulated line and is what drops the consumer to 94.4 degC on the low-flow day; 0.2 W/m2/K is the insulation class a 5 km 100 degC main needs. The return main is the same pipe type and trench as the supply main, so it carries the same insulation class; keeping the two equal keeps the network loss model consistent.
